chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"It is not valid for her to give herself in khul' (redemption) until she says to her husband: 'By Allah, I will not obey your oath, nor obey your command, nor perform ghusl for you from janabah, and I will surely make you lie on your bed with someone you dislike, and I will announce to you without your permission.' And indeed, people used to grant concession for less than this. So when the woman says that to her husband, it becomes valid for him to take what he took from her, and she remains with him having two divorces left, and the khul' counts as one divorce."
And he said: "The speech must come from her." And he said: "If the matter were up to us, we would not validate her divorce except for the waiting period (iddah)."
ai.seo_question: What are the specific verbal conditions required for a valid khul' divorce in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic debate regarding the necessity of specific verbal formulas (*lafz*) versus general intent (*ma'na*) in khul', with the Imam specifying that the declaration must originate from the wife to be valid. It establishes that khul' counts as one irrevocable divorce (*taliqah*), leaving two remaining, and notes the Imams' preference for delaying validity until the end of the waiting period (*iddah*) to ensure finality. This reflects the Shia emphasis on precise contractual conditions in marital dissolution, distinguishing it from the more flexible approaches found in other schools.
